title: Kotree
summary: The link-in-bio you are standing on — neobrutalist UI, an obfuscated guestbook, hidden easter eggs and an offline-first shell.

title: Portfolio
summary: My work showcase — selected projects, case studies and a downloadable resume, built as a static site with a Deno backend.

title: Offline first without a framework
summary: A service worker, a versioned cache and an IndexedDB queue cover most of what offline needs; the rest is deciding which failure to admit to.

title: View transitions in practice
summary: The native view transition API takes an afternoon to learn; the work is naming a few elements, respecting motion preferences and knowing where WebKit still differs.

title: React 19 and the external store
summary: Preferences and toasts live outside React, and useSyncExternalStore is the supported way to read them without tearing or hydration surprises.

title: MongoDB indexes that earn their keep
summary: The equality-sort-range rule explains most compound indexes; an audit script that runs the real query shapes explains the rest.

title: Case study: making Kotree fast
summary: A bundle diet, smaller hydration boundaries and a CI budget hold the home route at 663 kB of JavaScript and a 948 ms largest paint.

title: A CI that stays green
summary: A green build is a budget and a contract: fewer matrix jobs, honest retries, captured evidence and audit exceptions that expire.

title: Accessibility as a test, not a promise
summary: Every page runs through axe in the suite, and the contrast tokens, reduced-motion rules and keyboard routes are checked like any other feature.

title: Target size is a design constraint
summary: WCAG 2.2 sets a 24-pixel floor for pointer targets, and the spacing exception is narrower than most teams assume.

title: Case study: a guestbook that survives the internet
summary: An obfuscated wall, a spam score instead of a spam filter, database-backed limits and an offline queue that does not duplicate messages.

title: Locking down the page with a nonce
summary: Every response gets its own script nonce and a strict CSP, and violations land in the same stream as every other client error.

title: Fonts and the largest paint
summary: A font can delay the largest paint or shift the page after it; one preloaded subset and a matched fallback solve most of it.

title: A budget for every byte
summary: Every route has a raw-JavaScript ceiling checked in CI, and real visitors' p75 timings have their own shelf on the status page.

title: A service worker update people trust
summary: A waiting worker plus a visible refresh prompt is slower than skipWaiting and much less likely to lose someone's work.

title: Case study: a tip jar without a wallet library
summary: A handful of EIP-1193 calls, a hand-written wei parser and a deliberate list of things the tip jar does not do.

title: Search that works without JavaScript
summary: The server-rendered search page gives every result its own URL, and the command palette searches a build-time index of the content.

title: Building Win95 in React
summary: A fake desktop is a window manager with a dress code; the hard parts are focus, keyboard movement and keeping the drag off the React render path.

title: A database that tidies up after itself
summary: TTL indexes delete what has expired, rate limits live in the database across instances, and the audit log keeps a hashed record.

title: An AI terminal without a backend
summary: The terminal resolves commands locally, streams from a provider with the visitor's own key, and treats every answer as untrusted text.

title: Case study: shipping a Win95 desktop
summary: Four apps, one window manager and a scope list that kept the joke from becoming a second product.

title: Windows 95, maintained
summary: Notepad, Paint, Calculator and Minesweeper get the same care as everything else — snapping, keyboard nudging and real tests.

title: Webmentions for one person
summary: Receiving webmentions is a small endpoint and a large moderation job; for a personal site, RSS may already cover the same ground.

title: The real cost of a personal site
summary: The bill is small and the maintenance is not; the useful skill is deciding which features deserve a pager.

title: Test the boring things
summary: The restore drill, the secret scanner, the visual baselines and the post-deploy smoke test — dull checks that only matter on the bad day.

title: Secrets everywhere
summary: Fourteen easter eggs hide in Kotree, and a small counter now keeps score of how many you have found.

title: Offline, on purpose
summary: Kotree now survives a dropped connection — cached pages, a proper offline fallback and a queue that delivers your secrets later.

title: An offline guestbook
summary: Offline messages queue on the device, Background Sync delivers them with the tab closed, and no-JavaScript visitors get a straight answer.
